pageCache.pageTitle: Home - Hampden Gurney | Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
YOUR JOURNEY STARTS HERE
Hampden GurneyCofE Primary School
From our Headteacher, Evelyn Chua.
We are a one form entry Church of England primary school with approximately 240 pupils on role. The School has served the City of Westminster since 1863.
Our school’s vision is deeply rooted in its motivation to provide a first-class and spiritual experience for every child at Hampden Gurney. We want our children to be able to recognise their individual talents and gifts. We want them to shine with confidence, experience new challenges and be enriched by their thirst for knowledge and wisdom. Most of all, we want our children to be happy, resilient and reverent learners, and to be the best they can be.
Strong and steady leadership and governance is a key feature of the school’s success; a school led with a clear vision and direction. Hampden Gurney benefits from the dedicated and committed team of staff who are highly skilled, trained and motivated to provide the learning opportunities to enthuse and inspire our children.
Our curriculum is sequentially designed to develop children’s creative thinking skills, spirituality, self-confidence and the ability to build on what they have learnt before.
Inclusion is at the heart of the school. We pride ourselves in raising awareness of equalities and fundamental human rights, creating an inclusive and supportive learning environment. Our curriculum design is carefully considered to ensure that all our children will receive the skills, knowledge, norms and values to equip them for future society.
We work in partnership with parents and carers and very much value the support and contribution they make to the work and life of the school. The school also enjoys a close relationship with our Parish Church of the Annunciation. Because of our strong links between the home, school and parish, we are able to provide a happy, caring and inspirational learning environment, where all of our children can flourish and excel.
Our School Values
‘Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find.
Knock, and it will be opened for you.’ – Matthew 7:7
Our school vision is deeply rooted in the theology and Biblical teachings of Matthew 7:7 which speaks of the importance of prayer as a way of developing an enriched life and personal relationship with God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
At the heart of our school community is a commitment to prayer and worship. Our curriculum provides children with a thirst for knowledge and wisdom, a high level of challenge and a deep understanding that we are all equal and made in the image of God. Our relationships with each other, our local community and global companions leads us to want to care and serve others.

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values - Hampden Gurney | Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Hampden Gurney School is committed to working closely and in harmony with its community and celebrating the diversity of the UK. We aim to prepare children for life in modern Britain and to ensure that our school ethos, curriculum and approaches to teaching and learning reflect and promote British values.
We recognise that these values are not exclusive to being British and that they have come to be accepted throughout the democratic world as the method of creating an orderly society in which individual members can feel safe, valued and can contribute to for the good of themselves and others.
We work alongside our local community and recognise the variety of religious beliefs within it. We take children outside the school to take part in local events and meet different members of the community to appreciate the valuable contributions they make.
At Hampden Gurney C of E Primary School we uphold and teach pupils about the British Values which are defined as:
These values are taught explicitly through Personal, Social, Health, Citizenship and Emotional (PSHCE), and Religious Education (RE). We also teach the British Values through planning and delivering a broad and balanced curriculum.
The school takes opportunities to actively promote British Values through our daily collective worship and whole school systems and structures such as electing and running a successful School Council. We also actively promote the British Values through ensuring that our curriculum planning and delivery includes real opportunities for exploring these values.
At Hampden Gurney School, these values are reinforced regularly in the following ways:
Democracy – what do we do?
Help pupils to express their views
Rule of Law – what do we do?
Help pupils to distinguish right from wrong
Develop restorative justice approaches to resolve conflicts
Individual Liberty – what do we do?
Challenge stereotypes
Implement a strong anti-bullying culture
Follow the UNICEF rights respecting schools agenda
Respect and Tolerance – what do we do?
Promote respect for individual differences
Challenge prejudicial or discriminatory behaviour
Organise visits to places of worship
Develop links with faith communities
Develop critical personal thinking skills
Foundation Stage
As part of our daily set up Foundation Stage, pupils are taught the value of individual liberty through self-selecting their learning activities. Pupils are taught about the value of democracy through collaborative decision making, for example, during weekly Parliament time, pupils decide collaboratively what they like to learn the following week. They are learning to tolerate the different faiths and beliefs through their learning of the festivals, cultures and traditions and of other faiths through curriculum activities, stories, visits to special places of worship and religious education.
Our School Council 2025 – 2026
The School Council is a group of students who help students grow and express their views. Everyone has the chance to speak, no matter their age.
School council members meet once a week to discuss improvements to the school and how to involve younger children. We sometimes present a presentation to the class (each Key Stage 2 class has two representatives, and we are working to get younger children to be part of the school council, too) to see what they think and how the school can be improved.
The School Council helps children to have their say. On occasion, children who are not part of the school council are invited to one of their weekly meetings, to see how it works, and formulate new ideas. The School Council is a safe space for sharing ideas.
We are currently working towards making the school the best for everyone. We are starting the ‘School Council Surgery’, a surgery being a period of time that students visit the School Council to express ideas or share worries that we would attempt to fix. We believe that every idea is important, no matter who shared it.

pageCache.pageTitle: Collective Worship - Hampden Gurney | Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
“Our values determine the sort of person we are”
Collective worship is held each day except for Thursdays when there is a celebration of the Eucharist. Communion is led by Father Lincoln Harvey of the Church of the Annunciation, Marble Arch, who takes Mass with the support of a number of Year 6 pupils who act as servers. Pupils from Y2 – Y6 are encourage to offer a reading from the bible and offer prayers during the service.
Collective Worship is based upon the teachings of the Christian church but is inclusive, allowing space for all children to respond and reflect in their own way. When we gather as a school community on Fridays, we celebrate children’s achievements and learning with Certificates – not only for academic achievement but also for children who have demonstrated our school values.
At the heart of collective worship are the school collective worship values: Compassion, Creation, Endurance, Forgiveness, Friendship, Generosity, Hope, Humility, Justice, Peace, Reverence, Service, Thankfulness, Trust, Wisdom.
For further information visit www.christianvalues4schools.co.uk
Parents/Carers retain the right to withdraw children from R.E. and Collective Worship. This issue can be discussed with the Headteacher.

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision & Values - Hampden Gurney | Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our Vision
At the heart of our school community is a commitment to prayer and worship. Our curriculum provides children with a thirst for knowledge and wisdom, a high level of challenge and a deep understanding that we are all equal and made in the image of God. Our relationships with each other, our local community and global companions leads us to want to care and serve others.
In the Bible, we learn about the kind of people God wants us to be. We try to put this into practice in all that we do, and we encourage the children to do the same.
We live our vision through our Christian values of:
We teach children about reverence – a deep sense of love and respect for God – in all aspects of our school life but particularly in our Collective Worship, held daily in the school. Spending time every day to reflect on God’s word, helps the children to appreciate the gifts we are given, and builds a strong sense of purpose for our future lives.
We have an active partnership with the Annunciation, Marble Arch, and on Thursdays Father Lincoln comes to hold a whole school mass in school. The children play a vital role by preparing the altar, reading the lessons and acolyting during mass.
“But as he who called you is holy, you also be holy in all your conduct.”
Our planet is beautiful! As a community, our school gives thanks to God for the wonderful world we live in. Recently, our Courageous Advocates have been working on ways to help protect and sustain the environment. They have created The Action Group! (TAG) and have discussed deforestation, and plastic pollution during Collective Worship, and looked at some of the changes that we can make to improve our world.
‘TAG has taught me how to be confident and fight for what I believe to change the world for the better.’
“Therefore, as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in him, rooted and built up in him and established in the faith, just as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving.”
We often participate in the Bi-Borough Sports competitions throughout the year. Recently our team joined other schools in Regent’s Park in the Cross Country competition and our girls came 3rd! But more importantly, we learn about taking part, teamwork, celebrating the achievement of others and learning about good sportsmanship. By supporting each other and our peers, and encouraging them to do the best they can, we are all winners!
We are looking forward to more Sports Competitions this year, including the Swimming Gala, the Tennis Tournament, the Indoor and Outdoor Athletics and Basketball Competition. We consider behaviour, attendance and a good attitude when we invite children to take part and aim to involve every child in KS2.
“Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves.” (Philippians 2:3)
We teach children that forgiveness is fundamental to the character of God. Our Year 5 and 6 children can apply to be ‘Buddies’, mentoring the children in younger years at break and lunchtimes. By modelling good behaviour while playing games, they teach the younger children how to take turns, say sorry, and be friends after a disagreement, demonstrating our very important value: forgiveness!
“And forgive us our sins, for we ourselves forgive everyone who is indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation.”(Luke 11:4)
We teach children to believe in themselves, dare to try new things and persevere to reach their full potential.
When times get tough, we all need extra help and we are really fortunate to work with MIND UK. Our nominated Wellbeing Practitioner offers therapies and workshops to our whole school community. MIND also have many useful resources on their website https://www.mind.org.uk/
You’ll find more information about the work we do to encourage good mental health on our Wellbeing at Hampden Gurney page.
“And let us not grow weary of doing good, for in due season we will reap, if we do not give up.”(Galatians 6:9)
Our school thrives in the middle of a diverse, multi-cultural city. The values that have made London one of the best cities in the world, our British values – such as regard for the rule of law, participation in and acceptance of democracy, equality, free speech and respect for minorities – all work harmoniously with our Christian values.
We embrace these ideas in the work of our School Council. Our councillors act as representatives of their classmates, elected by their classmates, and discuss issues about the school with Mrs Chua and staff. In this way, our children learn that they have a voice, fundamental to living in a democracy. Working together, respecting each other as individuals, embracing diversity and overcoming challenges teaches our children how to live peacefully alongside one another.
“Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.”(Psalm 34:14)
“Peace and my faith” an artwork by Mirei. Winner of the First Prize for the Art and Poetry Competition from the City of Westminster.
We hope that this has given you a flavour of what our mission means in practice. It means happy children who feel welcomed and welcome others to their school. It is our aim to see that children are engaged with their learning, are excited by education and are motivated to achieve. We strive to teach our children to have respect for themselves and respect one another. By understanding the teachings of Christ, and living his message, our children know they are valued and will lead successful enriched lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Building Learning Power - Hampden Gurney | Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Building Learning Power
At Hampden Gurney we are passionately dedicated to our pupils becoming the best that they can possibly be. We believe that an ethos of ‘Building Learning Power’ enables all children, regardless of ability, to achieve their best.
“Term on term, year on year, a BLP school breeds young people who are more curious, more willing to take a risk and give it a go, more imaginative, more creative, more thoughtful, more ready, willing and able to learn with and through others. It’s developing this adventurous spirit that counts.”
Building Learning Power is an approach to learning to learn
Lifelong learning is our birth right. We can continually develop our capacity to learn throughout our lives. We are all learners every day of our lives it’s just that sometimes in our busy schedules we can lose sight of this wonderful capacity, worse still we can take it for granted and then assume that our children will just “pick it up”!
The 4 Learning Dispositions
1. RESILIENCE being ready, willing and able to LOCK ON TO LEARNING
2. REFLECTIVENESS being ready, willing and able to become MORE STRATEGIC ABOUT LEARNING
3. RESOURCEFULNESS being ready, willing and able to LEARN IN DIFFERENT WAYS
4. RECIPROCITY being ready, willing and able to LEARN ALONE AND WITH OTHERS

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Work with the Community - Hampden Gurney | Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Hampden Gurney Primary School is taking part in an exciting Arts Council’s Creativity Collaborative 3-year project.
We will be part of a network of schools across London to develop teaching for creativity, focusing on school culture, values and shared language. The London Creativity Collaborative network includes schools across all phases, including special education and 6th Form, and will tackle social and economic disadvantage, where creativity is needed most. The following partner organisations will enhance the project:
National TheatreV&AJohn Knowles Ritchie (JKR) – global design and branding agencyA New DirectionThe Creativity Collaborative programme emerged from the Durham Commission on Creativity and Education, a joint research collaboration between Durham University and Arts Council England, convened to look at the role creativity should play in the education of young people.
Partner schools working on the project:
Bushey Primary Education Federation, HertsEleanor Palmer Primary School, CamdenNetley Primary School, CamdenHampden Gurney Primary School, WestminsterThe St Marylebone CE Bridge School, WestminsterSt Mary’s and St John’s CE School, BarnetCentral Foundation Girls’ School, Tower HamletsDeptford Green School, LewishamThe Green School Trust, Hounslow
St Dominic’s Catholic Sixth Form College, HarrowTorriano Primary School, CamdenBrecknock Primary School, CamdenLady Margaret School, Hammersmith & FulhamThe St Marylebone CE School, Westminster
The project is led by The St Marylebone CE School, Westminster. They are coordinating the schools and partners, as well as working with Durham University to evaluate the three- year project. The 14 schools taking part have been divided into four sub-groups that will work closely together to trial teaching for creativity strategies.
What has happened so far?
We have attended the launch event and met all the schools and partner organisations taking part. We’ve also taken part in our first workshop with our sub-group of schools to develop a collective language around creativity and share our initial thoughts and plans for teaching for creativity. Strategies will be developed and trailed in the spring and summer term and over the next three years. Here are the latest updates.
Arts Council England. Read some more about the project here.
Hampden Gurney are proud to work with the following charities to raise awareness and hold fundraising events within the school.
Our Local Charity- Marylebone Project
This year we joined forces with the Annunciation, collecting food, cosmetics and toiletries for Harvest Festival. All these goodies were sent to the Marylebone Project to help them continue their amazing work.
Marylebone project was set up by the Church Army and The Portman House Trust, they provide long and short term beds to homeless women and offer essential facilities. The Marylebone Centre also delivers education, employment and training opportunities and meaningful activities in order to support service users into independent living.
Their value of spirituality is symbiotic with our own values as a school, to live full lives because God loves us all unconditionally.
If you would like to find out more about this charity, please take a look at their website
Anti-bullying Alliance – Odd Socks Day
This November we wore odd socks for Odd Socks Day!
On Monday 10 November we wore our Odd Socks because like the Anti-Bullying Alliance we believe that everyone needs an opportunity to express themselves and celebrate their individuality and what makes us all unique!
Thank you to all the children and staff for supporting this important and fun initiative. We raised £187 to donate the the Anti-Bullying Alliance to support their good work.
Christmas Jumper Day 2025
We all enjoy Christmas, we’re all partial to a Christmas Jumper but what we really love is Christmas Jumper day!
This year was no exception, the Christmas Jumpers went on in big style to celebrate our whole school Christmas. Thank you to all the families for giving so generously to this wonderful charity. We continue to applaud the amazing work of Save the Children and are so pleased to be able to contribute.
The Penfold Community Hub
Penfold Community Hub is a group within Westminster that offer stimulating and accessible activities to members of the community over 50. Their aim is to help people remain healthy, independent and active within their local community.
The school choir visited just before Christmas to sing carols with the residents and staff. We also enjoyed an afternoon tea with some fun colouring activities and chat.
This is an on-going initiative where children visit for a few hours to do different activities with the elderly. We hope our next visit will include the school orchestra.

Below you can read what two of our pupils had to say about the experience.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wellbeing at Hampden Gurney - Hampden Gurney | Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
At Hampden Gurney , we aim to provide children with the most comprehensive education possible. This includes a strong focus on developing, promoting and encouraging staff, pupils and families to embark on a journey towards healthy mental and emotional wellbeing.We want children to understand wellbeing is not about being ‘happy’, we want children to understand that we have many healthy experiences that are ‘good’ without any link to feeling happy.Children at Hampden Gurney, learn to understand that wellbeing is about our ability to make a contribution to our community, work productively, respond to challenges and bounce back and stay the course.Should you have any worries, concerns or just want to have a chat regarding wellbeing, please contact Ms Stefani
Wellbeing Award
In January, 2023, the school was awarded the Wellbeing Award for Schools!
‘Working together with our school community, Hampden Gurney was able to achieve this award by completing many different projects across the school which aimed to improve the wellbeing culture long-term. We are immensely grateful to everyone involved: children, staff, parents and governors, it would have been impossible without you. Hampden Gurney are committed to promoting and protecting positive emotional wellbeing and mental health and this award highlights are continued efforts to do so. We look forward to ensuring wellbeing remains a key focus for many years to come!’ – Miss Shin and Miss Macdonald, January 2023
There are eight objectives to achieve within the Wellbeing Award Framework, containing several Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) set out within each. The award focuses on ensuring effective practice and provision is in place that promotes the emotional wellbeing and mental health of both staff and pupils. The award will enable us to develop these practices where necessary and help us to ensure that wellbeing is embedded in the long-term culture of our school. It will help us to create an ethos where mental health is regarded as the responsibility of all.
With this award, we have demonstrated our commitment to:
Promoting the importance of mental health awareness
Wellbeing Ambassadors
Our children are just as keen as we are to ensure long-term, cultural change happens at Hampden Gurney. We had lots of children volunteering to help and decided to hold a democratic vote within our classes. Our Wellbeing Ambassadors have been appointed to take an active role in planning and delivering school wellbeing events, spreading the word and checking in on different groups of our school community.
Our Wellbeing Ambassadors for 2025-2026 are:
Y1- Hannah and Gabriel
Y2- Olivia and Jeannie
Y4- Thomson and Sophia
Y6- Charlotte and Daniel
When you need us…
Mental Health and Wellbeing are increasingly a central consideration within the school and within the wider community. Here at Hampden Gurney, we want to make life better for our children, remove any stigma around mental health and we do so by encouraging talk. A problem is halved when it is shared.
We have a number of different processes to help students who feel that they may need to talk to someone about their mental health or get the support for someone they are concerned about.
As a school, we take all aspects of a young person’s wellbeing seriously, but we are first and foremost a school. As well as contacting us to let us know your concerns, we strongly recommend that you contact your GP to discuss any serious concerns that you may have about your young person.
Should you need help with finding the right support, please see our wellbeing directory for signposting to local services and advice for parents.
The wellbeing of our families matters! We have arranged a schedule of workshops, as voted for by you, which we hope you will benefit from. Please check out the schedule to see if there are any of interest or even to check the dates for just a tea and a chat!
‘A great opportunity to meet other parents and socialise while doing something good for my health and wellbeing’
‘Brilliant for fostering community in the school.’
Thank you to all of our parents who joined us at our Maths Strategy Coffee Morning! We hope you found this useful and it helps you to support your children at home. We can’t wait for the next one!

“With an orchestra you are building citizens,
better citizens for the community.”
Music in Hampden Gurney plays a large role in our lives, and not only in lessons. Children across KS1 and KS2 have the opportunity to join the school orchestra and find a positive, guided and inspiring outlet for their musical talents.
We believe that playing in the school orchestra gives the children an opportunity to develop their social skills by making connections with the other students, and some of these interactions may develop into friendships that last a lifetime. They will be putting teamwork skills into practice as they become essential part of a functioning team that has clear goals. Playing their part well and with commitment will contribute to the performance of fine music together. Playing in an orchestra would help them develop a sense of responsibility, taking care of their instruments, rehearsing with resilience and passion. The commitment to practicing and improving can translate into their other school studies as well as helping them to cope with future life challenges. Cognitive skills are improved, from eye-hand coordination to concentration and visual recognition, as all are involved whilst children master the playing of one –or several!- instruments. They are building a strong skill-set that they can use going forward in their education and beyond while enjoying this creative musical space at school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome Message - Hampden Gurney | Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
A message from Fr Lincoln Harvey
I think Hampden Gurney School is an astonishing place. Anyone who visits immediately sees that our building is an architectural marvel. It is a breath-taking multi-storey hub of learning and discovery. However, not so many people realise that the building rises up from the altar in our basement chapel. And its design is no accident. The building captures the way in which the life of our school rests upon its Christian foundation. We are committed to prayer and worship, and I believe this provides our children with the best environment in which to flourish.
Hampden Gurney is of course open to children from every part of our local community. Our religious foundation determines our radically inclusive values, in which we seek to serve children whatever their belief or ability. We’re a very diverse community, much like a village school in size, but with the whole world attending. And diversity brings such riches to our community life, ensuring that the cultural capital of our lively neighbourhood finds expression in the day-to-day life of our school. It’s one of the reasons, I love spending time in school each week. I never fail to feel inspired by both the unity and diversity.
Hampden Gurney clearly places great value on academic excellence. We want our children to develop a genuine thirst for knowledge and wisdom, providing them with challenges that will lead to ever-deepening understanding. The evidence shows that the children reach their academic potential. For example, our recent national test (SATS) results were amazing. Year 6 pupils exceeded the national average in mathematics, reading, and writing, and this success shows how our children are deeply motivated to learn. I am often struck by their brilliance when I chat with them, with conversations venturing to just about any topic under the sun. But our children’s success depends on the wonderful team of teachers who serve in the school. Their passionate commitment to educational excellence shines bright. They work so hard to meet the needs of every child. The teachers really are an inspiring bunch.
But our school is not only about academic excellence. Our children have great fun, with sports, games, after-school clubs, and all manner of extra-curricular activities, such a music, chess club, and school trips. These activities are designed to fire the imagination, release creativity, and direct the children’s energy as they explore their world and embrace life to the full. And we take great care of them. Health and fitness is highly valued, with the children’s safety and well-being at the forefront of everything we do. Our children are in a great environment, of that I am sure.
Of course, Hampden Gurney School is led by the incomparable Mrs Chua. As headteacher, I think Mrs Chua embodies the school’s values: reverent, grateful, humble, and forgiving, she is resilience personified, whose joyful and energetic presence sets the tone for the entire school. She invests so much energy into making Hampden Gurney a happy and successful place, and leads the team of wonderful support staff and teachers by her example. It’s an absolute joy to work with her and be part of her amazing team.
And the Governing Body consists of such a wise group of dedicated volunteers, drawn from all walks of life. We are passionate about promoting high standards in educational achievement to help the school go from strength to strength. We are all very proud of our school, and – as this litany of praise suggests – I am absolutely delighted to be the new Chair of Governors. Thanks be to God for Hampden Gurney School!

pageCache.pageTitle: PSHE and RSE - Hampden Gurney | Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
The principle aim of the Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE) policy at Hampden Gurney School is to promote children’s personal and social development, including their health and well being.
“Today’s children and young people are growing up in an increasingly complex world and living their lives seamlessly on and offline. This presents many positive and exciting opportunities, but also challenges and risks. In this environment, children and young people need to know how to be safe and healthy, and how to manage their academic, personal and social lives in a positive way.”
At Hampden Gurney, we believe a strong home-school partnership is essential to supporting our young people and keeping an open door allows the conversation to flow and ensures we can provide our children the best Relationships and Health Education.
View our Skills and Progression Map below where you can find all vocabulary taught across the school.
A massive thank you to all parents who attended our recent workshop on PSHE in the classroom and the statutory framework for RSE!
Children and young people need the self-awareness, positive self-esteem and confidence to:
Our aim is that through the teaching of PSHE, pupils will learn to value their own achievements, deal with risk and meet challenges they will face and identify their values and strive to live up to them.
PSHE is reflected in the values and ethos of the school. The school’s curriculum embodies the values of self, relationships, society and the environment. Through emotional literacy, the school teaches children how to understand and express their emotions. It aims to develop sympathy, empathy, consideration, respecting and valuing others, sharing and co-operation, collaboration and negotiation skills, listening and responding appropriately, self-awareness and confidence.
Children’s personal and social development is enhanced through the school environment that allows them to feel safe and for which they have some responsibility. Social and moral responsibility is developed through encouraging positive behaviour and relationships, anti-bullying strategies, environment and recycling projects with local authorities. We currently have pupils involved in the School Council, an ‘Every Child Matters’ Team and a ‘Sustainable Schools’ Team.
The school’s Christian based assemblies provide daily opportunity to enhance pupils’ spiritual, moral, social and cultural development. It identifies, promotes and celebrates the school’s values and pupils’ achievements.
The “Hampden Gurney Values Flower” art project was accomplished with the joint effort of Reception Class, Years 1 and 2.
Teaching and Learning
A range of teaching strategies are used to provide effective learning opportunities for all pupils. These include an emphasis on active learning, enquiry, discussion and participation in citizenship activities. Teachers use circle time, drama and role play, art and craft, dance, music and stories to explore and express emotions.
Pupils develop their knowledge, skills and understanding by working together on school and community projects, making decisions, taking responsibility and reflecting on their experiences.
Partnership with parents and the local community
Work completed at school is aimed to complement the social and personal development of children provided at home. Working with parents is vital to our whole-school approach. Consultations with parents help develop better understanding between home and school and reinforce key points of learning. PSHCE is part of the Hampden Gurney ‘Home-School Agreement’ and provides broader links between the school and the parent community.

Meet the Governors
Hampden Gurney’s Governing Body works as a team with the Headteacher and the school staff, helping to provide a vibrant, imaginative and quality education for the children at the school.
Their contribution includes: agreeing the school’s aims, policies, targets and priorities, overseeing the financing of the school and helping to monitor the curriculum. There are two elected Parent Governors who are available to discuss any aspect of the Governing Body and a Clerk to the Governors, who can provide more information: please contact the school office.
Photographs of all Governors are on display outside the school office.
The two parent governors on the full governing body are Edit Laszlo and Abigail Goldsbrough.

The School Maintenance Fund
The School Maintenance Fund is vital element in ensuring that the School is a safe, well-equipped and pleasant environment for the children. This money is held and managed by the Governing Body and is used to make up short-falls in spending on maintaining and improving the school. As a Voluntary Aided Church School, the Governing Body is responsible for the school buildings and other capital works including the playgrounds and ICT infrastructure.

Support and nurture children’s musical development by offering broad musical experiences.
Providing musical activities that are imaginative, inspiring and fun, and that use singing and instrumental playing while corresponding to six areas of learning: Personal, social and emotional development; Communication, language and literacy; Mathematical development; Knowledge and understanding of the world; Physical development; Creative development.

Learning how to read rhythms and pitched notation and develop instrumental skills and co-ordination using singing, hand-held percussion instruments, and recorders.

pageCache.pageTitle: History of Hampden Gurney - Hampden Gurney | Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Hampden Gurney is a Church of England Voluntary Aided Primary School in the Diocese of London. It is a parochial school owned by private parish trustees, maintained by Westminster City Council and serves a wide Christian Community.
Hampden Gurney School was established in 1863 as a memorial to the Reverend John Hampden Gurney, former Vicar of St Mary’s, Bryanston Square. The first school building was situated on Hampden Gurney Street in the parish of the Church of the Annunciation, just north of Marble Arch and Oxford Street. In 1936 Hampden Gurney School was amalgamated with St Luke’s school (est 1860) located in Nutford Place. The new school operated over two campuses with infants and Juniors in Hampden Gurney St and seniors in Nutford Place. Unfortunately, St Luke’s church and school were destroyed during the Blitz in Sept 1940 and were never rebuilt. The vacant site became the new home of Hampden Gurney school which was opened by the poet John Betjeman, (who later became Poet Laureate) in 1967.
During the early 1990s, the school’s trustees set about planning the building of a new school with state of the art facilities to lead the way forward into the 21st century. Our current building is the culmination of these plans and provides the exciting, innovative, child and teacher friendly building which we now inhabit. The strong links with the Church of the Annunciation continue; Mass is led once a week by Father Lincoln Harvey, the current incumbent of the Annunciation, and we make a termly visit to the church. Father Lincoln is also the Chairman of the governing body of our school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art & Design - Hampden Gurney | Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
We believe Art and Design stimulate creativity and imagination. It provides visual, tactile and sensory experiences and a unique way of understanding and responding to the world around us.
Year 3 class, working collaboratively to create a large sculptural form
Pupils at Hampden Gurney are encouraged to explore ideas and meanings in the work of artists, craftspeople and designers, learning about the diverse roles and functions of art, craft and design in contemporary life and in different times and cultures.
When teaching Art and Design, our aims are:
As pupils progress through different topic areas, they have the opportunity to work independently as well as in collaboration with others. As well as creating individual masterpieces, pupils are also encouraged to comment on and suggest improvements to their own work, as well as that of others.
Art specialist
At Hampden Gurney, we are fortunate that we currently have a dedicated art teacher who works with pupils across Key Stage 2. Having an art specialist on-site has meant pupils have been able to gain in knowledge and experience from someone who has a real passion for the subject. Pupils have produced an increasingly wide range of excellent artwork using different materials and stimuli as starting points. Much of the work produced is displayed around the school or exhibited in the school’s annual art exhibition.
Local galleries
We are very fortunate living in the centre of London that we are so close to a range of museums and galleries. Pupils have taken part in a number of workshops at local galleries and exhibitions, enhancing art lessons at school.
Social Media
Work completed by the children is posted on Instagram. To view this page, please click on the icon.
Congratulations to Isabella N. in Year 6 for winning the Coronation Card Competition with her intricate drawing of the Coronation Crown. Isabella’s design has now been made into the card which will be posted by MP Nickie Aiken to Their Majesties The King and Queen Consort to wish them the very best on their Coronation on behalf of everyone across the City of London and Westminster. Although there can only be one winner, we are immensely proud of the creativity, skill and talent demonstrated by the Hampden Gurney children across all years. Well done everybody!
Back in 2019, Steve McQueen invited every Year 3 pupil in London to have their photograph taken by a team of specially trained Tate photographers. They included children from state primaries, independent schools, faith schools, special schools, pupil referral units and home-educated pupils. These class photos are brought together into a single large-scale installation, capturing tens of thousands of Year 3 pupils in a milestone year in their development.
“There’s an urgency to reflect on who we are and our future […] to have a visual reflection on the people who make this city work. I think it’s important and in some ways urgent.”Steve McQueen

pageCache.pageTitle: Computing - Hampden Gurney | Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Technology is a very important aspect of our daily lives. Teachers at Hampden Gurney recognise that it is important in today’s world that pupils should have a good knowledge and understanding of technology and how it can be used. Our teaching aims to develop pupils’ skills in using hardware and software, to develop their ability to use technology to support their use of language and communication, and to increase pupils’ awareness of the advantages and limitations of different forms of technology.
Our state of the art building is complemented by a computer suite situated on the upper floor of the building. All pupils have access to this facility, with each class timetabled in for a dedicated hour long session per week. In addition to this, teachers incorporate the use of technology into other areas of the curriculum, which enables pupils to see how the use of technology can be used in a wider context. We have a class set of laptops that are used regularly in class by pupils in Year 1 upwards. Each class is equipped with an interactive large screen TV, and recent additions have seen this equipment added to the library and our new meeting room.
Our aims at Hampden Gurney for Computing are:

Pupils in Key Stage 1 and 2 have their own access to Purple Mash, an on-line resource that is used by teachers to re-inforce and review concepts and ideas in a range of curriculum areas covered in school. Each pupil has an individual password and log-in which your child’s class teacher will be able to provide.
Security and Safety
All parents need to sign the Acceptable Use Policy (see resources section of the website), which clearly states expectations for pupils when using the internet as a resource at school.
Parent E-safety Information
From time to time, the school runs an e-safety workshop for parents in order to give advice about technology and how pupils can use it safely at school and at home. A helpful information sheet for parents can be found on Childnet’s ‘Know IT all’ website. As well as information on how to keep your children safe at home, it also highlights links to organistions that aim to protect children when they are using the internet.
These include: Childnet International’s website, Childnet’s digizen website which gives information about using social network and social media sites and CEOP (the Child Exploitation and Online Protection Centre’s) website.2Simple’s .
